item.description: WASHINGTON — The Space Development Agency is seeking industry proposals for a contract worth up to $369 million to expand the worldwide ground infrastructure supporting its constellation of low Earth orbit missile-warning and tracking satellites.

item.title: Ukraine’s Starlink experience offers a lesson for the Pentagon
item.description: For some time now, the Ukrainian government has been seeking SpaceX’s authorization for the use of Starlink up to 200 kilometers inside Russia. Starlink has long provided high-speed connectivity to soldiers on the frontline, and Starlink terminals mounted on drones have been crucial to the “middle strike” campaign launched this spring, which involves the targeting of logistical routes into Crimea and military bases on the peninsula annexed by Russia. Musk, however, has reportedly had concerns that authorizing its use so deep inside Russian territory would amount to an escalation. Zelenskyy has since awarded Musk the Order of Freedom , one of Ukraine’s highest state honors, which can justifiably be seen as a bid to get him to change his mind.

item.description: PARIS — The satellite industry is coming to grips with SpaceX’s plans to end commercial Falcon 9 launches in the next few years, creating a significant, if temporary, gap in access to orbit.

item.title: Pentagon Plans Phased Golden Dome Buildout Through 2035
item.description: WASHINGTON — Gen. Michael Guetlein, head of the Golden Dome missile defense program, said the Pentagon is taking a two-stage approach, planning to stitch together existing military systems for an initial missile shield in 2028 before transitioning to a more affordable architecture designed specifically for homeland defense by 2035.

item.title: Space Force expands use of commercial satellites to track electronic interference
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Space Force is expanding the use of commercial satellites to detect and locate GPS jamming and other electronic interference, turning what began as an experiment into a standing global operation.

item.title: Rocket Lab continues high Electron cadence with Synspective launch
item.description: PARIS — Rocket Lab launched a radar-imaging satellite for Japanese company Synspective on Sept. 18 on the fifth flight of its Electron rocket in a month and a half.

item.title: Ghgsat To Improve Methane Detection With Second Generation Satellite
item.description: PARIS – GHGSat’s second-generation satellite, unveiled Sept. 21, is twice as sensitive in detecting methane emissions while providing double the monitoring capacity of the Canadian firm’s original satellites.

item.title: Sedaro gets $45 million in Space Force funding to expand mission analysis software
item.description: WASHINGTON — Space software company Sedaro will receive up to $45 million in government funding to expand a platform that helps the U.S. Space Force analyze how different satellites, sensors and other capabilities perform together.

item.title: Jamming created a resilience market. The space industry is losing it to the ground.
item.description: In the first quarter of this year, roughly 978,000 maritime GPS jamming events were recorded worldwide. Ninety-eight percent of them happened in one place: the Middle East Gulf. It is the largest single-quarter concentration of maritime jamming ever recorded, and more than 1,100 vessels in the region were affected.
